title: How to review your hands
summary: Reviewing after play is the fastest way to improve.

why.text: At the table there is no time to think long. After playing you can calmly go over your decisions and find repeated mistakes, **leaks**. One fixed leak is often worth more than dozens of hours played.

how.text:
How to review:
- While playing, flag tough hands **"to review"**.
- Start with **big pots** and close decisions, not with every hand.
- In the replayer, stop before each of your decisions and ask: "What did I know at this point? Which hands could the opponent have?"
- Look at the **hand analysis**: where a decision is marked as an inaccuracy or a mistake, and why.
- Write down **one leak** and work on it in the next sessions, rather than everything at once.

q-review.q: Which hands should a review start with?
options: All of them from the first
q-review.explain: Big pots and tough decisions affect results the most.

options: A repeated mistake in your game
t1.explain: A leak is a habitual mistake that steadily costs chips.

t2.q: What is the key question when reviewing a decision?
options: What cards did the opponent really have?
What did I know then, and which hands could the opponent have?
t2.explain: A decision is judged by the information available when it was made.

t3.q: How many leaks should you work on at once?
t3.explain: Working on one leak at a time gives a visible result instead of spreading thin.
